headline: State desk: Virginia hospitals get cannabis rules; Texas bill talks
dek: Virginia hospital staff may give patients medical cannabis from 16 December, while lawmakers in Texas, Georgia and Kentucky line up 2027 marijuana bills.
key_points: Virginia's final hospital rules, published on 16 November, let authorised hospital staff store, dispense and give cannabis oil to certified patients from 16 December.
Texas Rep. John Bucy says talks with House leaders on his HB 362 legalisation bill are productive, and that the incoming lieutenant governor is prioritising the issue.
Georgia Rep. Eric Bell plans a decriminalisation bill after Democrats won the state House and governor's office; Republicans kept the Senate 29 to 27.
Kentucky Sen. Gary Clemons will refile his decriminalisation and expungement bill but says he has no Republican support.
body: Virginia has finished the rules that let hospitals handle medical cannabis for their patients, and lawmakers in three Southern states are lining up marijuana bills for 2027 after this month's elections. Here is what moved, and what each change means.

The common thread is timing. Most of these proposals were filed or promised in the two weeks since the 3 November elections, and each now faces a 2027 session in which at least one chamber is still controlled by the party that has blocked reform.
## Virginia: hospitals may give cannabis oil from 16 December

Virginia's final hospital regulations were published in the Virginia Register of Regulations on 16 November and take effect on 16 December, The Marijuana Herald reported. Hospital employees who are already allowed to possess, distribute or give medicines may also store, dispense and administer cannabis oil to patients holding a valid written certification under the state's medical programme.

The rules carry out HB 75 and SB 332, passed in April, which protect qualifying medical staff from prosecution under specified state drug laws when they handle medical cannabis for authorised patients. Those laws also cover nursing homes, hospices and assisted living facilities; the new rules deal only with hospitals. Although the bills grew out of concern for terminally ill patients, the hospital rule applies to any certified patient, the Herald said. The State Health Commissioner approved the action in August on behalf of the Board of Health.

Why it matters: hospital admission has been a gap in access, since a certified patient could lose their medicine at the door. The rules give hospitals a written framework, though each hospital still decides how it implements them. As we reported on 17 November, Virginia's cannabis commission is also preparing proposals for the 2027 session.
> The election did not legalise anything. It moved bills from dead on arrival to dead in one chamber.
## Texas: Bucy says talks are productive

Rep. John Bucy, an Austin Democrat, told The Marijuana Herald he is working with stakeholders on a legalisation framework and having productive talks with House leaders. His HB 362 would let adults 21 and older possess up to two ounces and grow up to 12 plants at home, and would set up licensed retailers, growers, labs and transporters. His HB 507 would bar most state and local government employers from requiring a negative marijuana test, with exceptions including police and federally regulated transport jobs.

Bucy said Lieutenant Governor-elect Vikki Goodwin, a Democrat, is prioritising the issue. Democrats won the House and the governor's office in November, the Herald reported, while Republicans kept the Senate. The Legislature convenes on 12 January 2027, and neither bill has had a hearing. As we reported on 10 November, Democrats pre-filed legalisation bills in both chambers.

Rep. Eric Bell, a Democrat from House District 75, told The Marijuana Herald he will introduce a decriminalisation bill in 2027 and expects some form of decriminalisation or legalisation to follow the election. Democrats won control of the Georgia House for the first time in more than two decades and the governor's office, with Keisha Lance Bottoms elected, but Republicans held the Senate by 29 to 27, the Herald reported.

Today, possessing an ounce or less is a misdemeanour carrying up to 12 months in jail and a $1,000 fine. Bell co-sponsored HB 1248 this year, a full legalisation bill that stalled in committee. Georgia's medical market is moving on its own track: as we reported on 17 November, one licensed seller has begun home delivery by mail.
## Kentucky: a bill with no Republican backing

Sen. Gary Clemons, a Democrat, said he will refile his decriminalisation and expungement bill, but told the Herald that Republicans have not offered support. His 2026 version, SB 164, would have removed penalties for adults 21 and older possessing up to an ounce of flower, five grams of concentrate or five plants, protected people on probation or parole, and created a fee-free expungement path. It was referred to the Senate Committee on Committees on 5 February and never got a hearing.

Watch Virginia hospitals' policies as the rules take effect on 16 December. Watch the Texas Senate, where any legalisation bill would need Republican votes after the session opens on 12 January. And watch Georgia's narrow Senate, where two or three Republican votes would decide whether decriminalisation moves.
